An open-source research platform for evaluating graph-based money-mule detection and investigator review. It combines a streaming backend, shared as-of features, model evaluation and auditable decisions. It is not a production fraud-prevention service.
Are the results from real bank transactions?

No. The published evidence comes from simulated datasets, including PaySim and a local typology generator. PaySim evaluates contemporaneous transaction classification, not future account or ring detection. No recovery or real-world financial benefit has been measured.
Does it connect directly to I4C or NCRP?
No. The watchlist provider is a simulated I4C/NCRP-style adapter. MuleNet has no direct access to those systems and makes no claim of an official partnership or regulatory approval.
Does a suspicious score automatically freeze an account?
No bank account is frozen by this project. SOFT_HOLD is a time-limited internal review state with release and review paths. A score is a signal to investigate, not a finding of guilt.
Can I deploy this in production?

Not as a production decision system. Security acceptance has failed on documented unresolved findings, the legacy investigator UI needs API migration, and full deployment-scale acceptance is unfinished. This public website exposes none of the scoring, ingestion or case-management endpoints.
Can I run or contribute to the research?

Yes. Start with the repository README, data-license notes and contribution guide. Dataset access is separate from the code license. Synthetic runs require an explicit opt-in, and generated reports must retain their provenance and limitations.
Research with its limits in view.
